attacks.claim: The launch announcement claims zero fees on options with no fine print, but the release notes say options carry a $0.50/contract fee and SEC and FINRA TAF fees apply to sells. This is a false, unbalanced public communication that violates the agreed FINRA 2210 fair-and-balanced requirement.
attacks.evidence: "trade stocks, ETFs **and options** with zero commissions and zero fees. No catches, no fine print." vs. release notes: "options contract fee lowered to $0.50 per contract ... Regulatory fees (SEC, FINRA TAF) still apply to sells."

attacks.claim: Migration 0148 irreversibly drops legacy_legs at 06:00 before any v5 verification. The rollback target v4.18.2 reads legacy_legs, so rolling back after that point cannot work. This breaks the agreed 30-minute rollback SLO, and the claim that no down path is needed is wrong.
attacks.evidence: "ALTER TABLE order_templates DROP COLUMN legacy_legs;" and "Migrations are forward-only; no down migrations are needed for this release." alongside "kubectl rollout undo deploy/orders-svc` to v4.18.2" and "4.x orders-svc template endpoints" reading legacy_legs.

attacks.claim: Migration 0147 adds legs_json as NOT NULL with no default, and applies before v5 deploys. Live v4.18.2 orders-svc pods and 4.18.2 app clients (which keep running for up to 7 days during phased rollout) still write only legacy_legs, so new template inserts will fail the constraint.
attacks.evidence: "ALTER TABLE order_templates ALTER COLUMN legs_json SET NOT NULL;" with rollout "1. 06:00 ET apply migrations 0147, 0148." and "2. 06:10 ET deploy orders-svc v5.0.0 (rolling, 12 pods)."

attacks.claim: The migration runs a full-table UPDATE of ~2.9M rows and then SET NOT NULL (a full scan under an exclusive lock) inside one transaction on a live table. The 41s dry run on a snapshot omits concurrent write load and lock blocking on template reads and writes.
attacks.evidence: "Migration 0147 dry run against a prod snapshot (2.9M templates): 41s, 0 conversion errors." and the migration body: "UPDATE order_templates SET legs_json = legacy_legs_to_json(legacy_legs);" followed by "ALTER COLUMN legs_json SET NOT NULL;"

attacks.claim: Backward compatibility during the rolling deploy is unspecified. The artifact does not say whether v5.0.0 keeps serving the legacy template endpoints that 4.18.2 clients call, so mixed-version traffic for 6 to 7 days is unverified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any statement that v5.0.0 serves the 4.x template endpoints. Only "2. 06:10 ET deploy orders-svc v5.0.0 (rolling, 12 pods)." and "Mobile: ... 5.0 clients fall back to hiding Reorder if `/v5/templates` returns 404."

attacks.claim: The smoke test places a real order on a live house account at 06:30 ET, before the market opens and before any rollback decision point. It is a real-money action on a release whose rollback path is already broken.
attacks.evidence: "3. 06:30 ET smoke test with house accounts in the paper environment and one live house account."

attacks.claim: The launch post, scheduled for 09:00 ET, tells users to update today. The App Store ramp is 7 days and Play goes 5% to 100% over 6 days, so most users cannot get 5.0 that day. The post overpromises availability.
attacks.evidence: "Update the app today." vs. "Mobile: App Store phased release (7-day ramp) and Play staged rollout 5% → 20% → 50% → 100% over 6 days."

attacks.claim: There is no evidence that a registered principal approved the retail communication before first use under FINRA 2210, or that customers were notified of the options fee change before it takes effect.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: principal approval record for the blog/X announcement and any customer notice or fee-schedule update for the options fee change from $0.65 to $0.50.

attacks.claim: The claim of always landing on the review sheet with a live quote is contradicted by the closed-market behavior, which prefills a last-close quote and converts market orders to limit.
attacks.evidence: "You always land on the review sheet with the live quote and estimated cost" vs. "If the market is closed, Reorder prefills but ... defaults market orders to limit at last close."

attacks.claim: Reorder prefills the same symbol and quantity for filled options orders, but the artifact does not address expired or closed contracts, so prefill could target an invalid instrument.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: handling of Reorder for expired or closed options contracts. QA lists "2/3/4-leg options" pass but no expiry case.

attacks.claim: The dark-mode chart axis label fix has no contrast verification, and the accessibility claim covers only screen-reader behavior.
attacks.evidence: "Accessibility: VoiceOver/TalkBack pass on History and Reorder review sheet." vs. "dark mode chart axis labels" with no contrast check listed.

attacks.claim: The options fee cut lowers revenue per contract, but the artifact gives no revenue impact or budget math for the change.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: revenue impact estimate for "options contract fee lowered to $0.50 per contract (was $0.65)."
